maml:description.maml:para: Converts an image file to a data uri that can be embedded in an HTML page

The ConvertTo-clNovaHtmlDataUri cmdlet reads an image file & returns it as a base64 data uri (data:image/png;base64,...) so the image is part of the HTML file & is also shown when the computer is offline
The supported files are png, jpg, jpeg, gif, svg, webp, & ico
This is an internal helper function that is used by the public functions
The path of the image file

The ConvertTo-clNovaHtmlEncoded cmdlet HTML encodes the string value of an object so that characters such as < > & " ' are shown as text & can not change the HTML of a report
A null value returns an empty string
This is an internal helper function that is used by the public functions
The value to encode, the string value of the object is encoded

maml:description.maml:para: Replaces the {{Name}} tokens of an HTML template with values

The Expand-clNovaHtmlTemplate cmdlet replaces every {{Name}} token of a template with the value of the same name in the Token hashtable
The tokens are replaced in one pass, so a {{Name}} text inside of a value is never replaced again. A token without a value is replaced with an empty string
The values are NOT encoded, encode text values with ConvertTo-clNovaHtmlEncoded before adding them to the Token hashtable
This is an internal helper function that is used by the public functions
The text with the {{Name}} tokens

Calculates how many summary cards are placed in each row

The Get-clNovaCardLayout cmdlet calculates the number of summary cards per row so that every row has the same number of cards
2 rows with 6 cards -> 3 cards on the top row & 3 on the bottom row 3 rows with 12 cards -> 4 cards on each of the 3 rows
The number of rows is the minimum number of rows needed with the MaxPerRow limit. The cards per row is then the number of cards divided by the rows. When the cards can not be divided evenly (7 cards) the last row is shorter
The layout is calculated for desktops (Xl), tablets (Md), & phones (Sm)
This is an internal helper function that is used by the public functions
The number of summary cards
The most cards that are allowed on one row of a desktop screen
Default value: 4
The most cards that are allowed on one row of a tablet screen
Default value: 2

maml:description.maml:para: Gets an inline SVG icon for an HTML report

The Get-clNovaHtmlIcon cmdlet returns a Bootstrap Icon as inline SVG so that the icon works in an offline report & does not need a font or an internet connection
The icons are the svg files in the icons folder of the report resources (build\HtmlReport\icons). The Update-HtmlResources.ps1 build script downloads them
When the icon does not exist the info-circle icon is returned. An empty string is returned when there are no icons at all
This is an internal helper function that is used by the public functions

maml:description.maml:para: Finds a resource file (template, css, js, icon, or data file) of the module

The Get-clNovaResourcePath cmdlet finds the full path of a resource file that is shipped with the module
The module is used from two places & the resources are in a different place in each - Source module : build\HtmlReport (next to the module folder) - Built module : <module folder>\HtmlReport
The folders above the file that calls the function are searched for the relative path, first as <folder>\<RelativePath> & then as <folder>\build\<RelativePath>

maml:description.maml:para: Creates a modern, mobile friendly HTML report from PowerShell objects

The New-clNovaHtmlReport cmdlet turns any PowerShell objects into a single HTML file with a dark sidebar & header, an off white body, summary cards, & a sortable, searchable table
The design is based on SB Admin 2 (ported to Bootstrap 5.3) & works on desktops (Windows, Linux, & macOS) as well as on Android & iOS phones & tablets
By default everything needed (Bootstrap, the theme, the icons, & the scripts) is embedded in the file so the report works offline. Use -ResourceMode Cdn to link the Bootstrap 5.3 CDN files instead which makes the file smaller
The pieces of the report are also available as separate functions which can be used to build other reports - New-clNovaHtmlSummaryCardSet & New-clNovaHtmlSummaryCard - New-clNovaHtmlTable

Only used with BrandLogoPath. BrandLogoPath is shown when the sidebar is expanded. A square image works best

The logo is embedded in the report, so it is also shown when the computer is offline. The icon & the name are used as the alternative text. When the sidebar is collapsed only the left part (the symbol) of the logo is shown unless BrandLogoCollapsedPath is used

maml:description.maml:para: Creates the HTML of one summary card

The New-clNovaHtmlSummaryCard cmdlet creates the HTML of a single summary card for an HTML report. A summary card shows one quick fact about the data in the report such as a total, a percentage, or a link
A card can show a progress bar (Percent), a small note, an icon, & a tooltip. A card with a Url is a link
The cards are placed on the page with New-clNovaHtmlSummaryCardSet which creates evenly filled rows of cards. The HTML needs the Celerium.Nova report css to look right, use New-clNovaHtmlReport to create a complete page
The color of the card border, title, & progress bar
Acceptable values: 'Primary','Success','Info','Warning','Danger','Secondary','Dark'
Default value: Primary
The name of a Bootstrap Icon to show on the card
Default value: clipboard-data
Icons that can be used are listed in build\HtmlReport\resources.json
A small line of text shown below the value
Shows a progress bar that is filled with this percentage (0 - 100)
The HtmlReport folder to read the templates & icons from
By default the folder of the module is used
The title of the card
The text that is shown when the mouse is over the card
Makes the card a link. Only http, https, mailto, & page (#) links are allowed

maml:description.maml:para: Creates the HTML of a group of summary cards that are laid out in evenly filled rows

The New-clNovaHtmlSummaryCardSet cmdlet creates the HTML of any number of summary cards & scales the layout to fit them. Every row has the same number of cards
6 cards -> 2 rows of 3 cards 12 cards -> 3 rows of 4 cards
At most MaxPerRow cards are placed on one row of a desktop screen, tablets show 2 cards per row, & phones show 1 card per row. A row that can not be filled evenly (for example 7 cards) is centered
Every card is defined by a hashtable or an object with the same properties as the parameters of New-clNovaHtmlSummaryCard (Title, Value, Note, Percent, Color, Icon, Tooltip, & Url)
One or more cards, hashtables or objects with the properties of New-clNovaHtmlSummaryCard
Example: @{ Title = 'Total'; Value = 23; Icon = 'laptop' }

maml:description.maml:para: Creates the HTML of a sortable, searchable table card from PowerShell objects

The New-clNovaHtmlTable cmdlet converts PowerShell objects into the HTML of a table card for an HTML report
The table - Can be sorted by clicking any column header (numbers, dates, & text are sorted correctly) - Can be searched & shows a configurable number of rows per page - Highlights the entire row when the mouse is over it - Scrolls sideways on small screens instead of breaking the page
Only the properties in the Property parameter are shown (in that order). When it is not used the first 8 properties of the first object are shown so that the table fits on a typical monitor without a lot of horizontal scrolling
All values are HTML encoded. The sorting, search, & paging are done by the script of the Celerium.Nova report (build\HtmlReport\js\Celerium.Nova.js) which New-clNovaHtmlReport adds to the page
Hashtable of a property name & the column title to show for it
Example: @{ OSVersion = 'OS Version'; EndOfSupport = 'End Of Support' }

Default value: yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm

Default value: psn-table

Default value: 10

By default the first 8 properties of the first object are used

By default the folder of the module is used
